name: Tessera Industries Metamaterial Cloak Rounds MCR-1 'Vanishing Act'
description: Rifle ammunition coated with a metamaterial shell that renders the projectile effectively invisible in flight. The MCR-1 round is a standard 7.62mm projectile encased in a metamaterial jacket that bends visible light around the round as it travels, making it undetectable by optical tracking systems and the human eye. The round is still detectable by radar and thermal sensors, but in practical terms, targets cannot see the bullet coming and optical-based defense systems cannot track it. The metamaterial jacket ablates on impact, leaving a standard wound channel with no exotic trace evidence. Tessera developed it for sniper applications where muzzle flash and bullet trace are the primary indicators of shooter position.
specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm metamaterial-jacketed
optical invisibility: Visible light bending jacket, effective in flight
radar detectability: Standard — metamaterial does not affect radar signature
thermal detectability: Standard — metamaterial does not affect thermal
effective range: 100-800 meters
metamaterial ablation: Complete on impact
weight per round: 12g
compatibility: Standard 7.62mm rifle platforms
story_hooks: A target was killed by a 7.62mm round that no witness saw and no optical security system detected in flight — only the impact was recorded, making the shooter's position untraceable.
Tessera's metamaterial jacket technology has been reverse-engineered and someone is applying it to larger munitions — RPG warheads that cannot be seen until they hit.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively ordinary-looking rifle round with a subtle iridescent sheen. At rest, the projectile appears to shimmer faintly as light refracts across its metamaterial jacket—almost ghost-like. The casing is standard brass, but the jacket catches light in ways that feel unnatural, as if the round exists slightly out of phase with reality.
physical_description.dimensions: 56mm overall length, 7.62mm diameter projectile body, 8mm jacket width at widest point
physical_description.weight_description: Slightly heavier than standard 7.62mm rounds due to the metamaterial coating—noticeably dense and substantive in the palm, yet balanced
physical_description.primary_material: Brass casing, steel/tungsten core projectile, metamaterial composite jacket (proprietary Tessera lattice structure)
physical_description.finish: Polished brass casing with faint factory markings; metamaterial jacket has an opalescent, oil-slick finish that shifts between gunmetal gray, violet, and deep teal depending on viewing angle
physical_description.color_scheme: Burnished brass base with metamaterial jacket rendering in iridescent gray-violet-teal spectrum; primer cup is matte black
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth brass casing, slightly waxy from protective coating; metamaterial jacket has an almost tacky, micro-textured surface—deliberately grippy to prevent accidental slippage during loading
distinctive_features: Iridescent metamaterial jacket with visible light-bending distortion effect
Micro-etched Tessera Industries logo on jacket (faintly visible only at certain angles)
Faint thermal management grooves running lengthwise along the jacket
Slightly asymmetrical jacket seam where metamaterial wrapping meets projectile base
Primer cup recessed deeper than standard rounds—ablation containment feature
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Industries maker's mark stamped on brass casing near the primer; batch number laser-etched on jacket (visible only with raking light). No serial numbers—mass-produced prohibited ammunition
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine in box, but cosmetically fragile—the metamaterial jacket shows microscopic stress fractures and discoloration when stored improperly. Field-worn specimens show dulled iridescence and edge wear on the jacket seam
